correctness.rationale: For a full-support two-dimensional evolution algebra with M=[[a,b],[c,d]], nonzero determinant gives A^2=A and the established perfect=>semiprime theorem. For zero determinant, e2^2=(b/a)e1^2 and every nonzero ideal I contains A^2=Kv: if x=u e1+w e2 is nonzero, multiply by a basis idempotent-factor to isolate a nonzero multiple of v. Hence semiprime iff v^2 !=0. Exactly v^2=(a^2+bc^2/a)v, giving defect a^3+bc^2=0; a complete two-loop graph is downward-directed, so source Corollary 3.15 yields equivalence with primeness. For F_q, d=bc/a on the rank-one locus; each a,c!=0 fixes b=-a^3/c^2,d=-a^2/c, so precisely (q-1)^2 nonsemiprimes, (q-1)^3(q-2) perfect, (q-1)^2(q-2) semiprime nonperfect and q(q-2)(q-1)^2 semiprime. Independent explicit ideal-subspace enumeration for q=2,3,5,7 confirms each formula, not used as arbitrary-field proof.
residual_risks: Counts structure matrices with a specified natural basis, not isomorphism classes; arbitrary-field proof needs abcd!=0.
Finite q enumerations are supportive, not proof for all fields.
